issue.title: Proc-backed running monitor with no recorded pid is never reconciled after its supervisor dies
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-1sd.3 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #3) of epic sase-1sd; filed by the
sase-1sd land agent on 2026-11-12 after re-verifying on athena.

Live example: monitor `gvw2ee77qc5a` (member `sase-1ih.2--mon-0`, lane `sase-1ih.2`,
command `sase tool run check`, label `tool:check (joined)`), started
2026-10-09T00:10:39Z. On 2026-11-12, `sase monitor list -a -j` still reports
`monitor_state: running`, `is_terminal: false`, `pid: null`, `exit_code: null`,
`followup_outcome: null`, elapsed ~35 days, with a stale `next_action`. Its
`agent_meta.json` has `monitor_state=running`, `monitor_settled=false`, `pid=None`,
`proc_id=gvw2ee77qc5a`, and there is no `done.json`. `sase proc show gvw2ee77qc5a` says
no proc matches. The host has rebooted at least twice since then (11-01, 11-07).

Root cause (from source): `should_reconcile_dead_supervisor` in
`src/sase/monitor/reconcile.py` returns False as soon as `record.pid is None`, before
both the `named_proc_owns(...)` check and the `_is_pre_reboot_monitor(...)` check. A
proc-backed monitor (`proc_id` set) whose proc died before a supervisor pid was recorded
is therefore never reconciled: not by liveness, not by a missing proc, and not by
reboot. The member stays `running` forever, its artifact stays half-settled, and
`settle_claim_and_followup` never runs.

Repro: build a MonitorRecord with `monitor_state="running"`, `pid=None`, a `proc_id`
with no entry in the proc snapshot, and a pre-reboot or cold start time.
`should_reconcile_dead_supervisor` returns False. Expected: it reconciles the record as
lost or dead-supervisor, the same way a dead pid is handled.

Fix shape: when `pid is None`, settle the monitor as lost if it predates the current
boot, or if its `proc_id` has no live owning proc and a start grace window has passed.
Keep a fresh pid-less monitor that is still starting up (inside grace, or proc live)
untouched, and add regressions for all three cases. Sase-1sd.3 already made the
stranded-work classifier strand the dead member (sase-core afc64b10). This bead covers
the settlement half, which that phase left open.

task_type_fields.impact: Proc-backed monitors whose proc died before recording a supervisor pid stay running forever across reboots; their follow-up and claim settlement never runs and the monitor list shows them as live.
task_type_fields.repro: Running MonitorRecord with pid=None and a proc_id absent from the proc store (live example gvw2ee77qc5a on athena) is never reconciled; should_reconcile_dead_supervisor returns False before the proc-ownership and pre-reboot checks.

issue.creation_reason: Phase sase-1sd.3 found monitor gvw2ee (sase-1ih.2--mon-0) stuck running with no pid for 35 days. The sase-1sd landing traced it to the pid-None short-circuit in should_reconcile_dead_supervisor, which the stranded-work classifier fix did not address.

payload.description: sase-1sd.3 fixed the classifier half (dead pending monitors strand); this bead is the settlement half for pid-less proc-backed monitors
Adjacent orphaned-monitor settlement surface: 1ra.8 settles staged monitors whose adopter died; this bead settles running proc-backed monitors with no pid
